result.abstract: The lecture describes the larynx as a box of nine cartilages joined by joints, ligaments and membranes, with intrinsic muscles that abduct, adduct, tense and relax the vocal cords and extrinsic muscles that move the larynx in swallowing. It covers the compartments and histology of the laryngeal cavity, its arteries, veins, lymphatics and the superior and recurrent laryngeal nerves, and the physiology of phonation. Clinical correlations include laryngeal nerve damage, laryngeal obstruction with the Heimlich manoeuvre, and vocal nodules.

concepts.name: Larynx
concepts.definition: The upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice: an unpaired median tube of cartilages linked by joints, muscles and ligaments and lined by mucous membrane. It acts as a sphincter at the inlet of the lower respiratory tract, extends from the upper border of the thyroid cartilage at C4 to the lower edge of the cricoid at C6, and serves phonation, respiration, protection and deglutition.

evidence.quote: The larynx is the upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice, also called the organ of phonation
Larynx extends from the upper thyroid cartilage at C4 to the lower cricoid at C6
It acts as a sphincter at the inlet of lower respiratory tract

concepts.name: Thyroid cartilage
concepts.definition: A large unpaired cartilage of the larynx shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae. Its thick posterior margin is extended by superior and inferior cornua, the inferior carrying a cricoid articular surface.

evidence.quote: Shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae
Three unpaired and large: thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis

concepts.name: Cricoid cartilage
concepts.definition: An unpaired signet-shaped ring of cartilage with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at the level of C6. It is the only cartilage that completely encircles the lumen of the larynx and is called the foundation stone of the larynx.

evidence.quote: The only cartilage that completely encircles the lumen of the larynx, and the foundation stone of the larynx
The cricoid is the only complete ring in the airway, at C6, the foundation stone of the larynx.
This is a signet-shaped ring of cartilage with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina

concepts.name: Epiglottis
concepts.definition: An unpaired cartilage of the larynx shaped like a tennis racket with a curved lower handle forming its foot. Its laryngeal (posterior) side faces the vestibule, its lingual (anterior) side faces the base of the tongue and hyoid, and its foot inserts into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage through the thyroepiglottic ligament.

evidence.quote: Shaped like a tennis racket with a curved lower handle forming its foot
Shape: tennis racket with curved lower handle forming the foot of the epiglottis

concepts.name: Arytenoid cartilage
concepts.definition: A paired cartilage of the larynx shaped like a triangular pyramid about 15 mm high. Its apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage and its concave base with the cricoid lamina; the base carries the vocal process and the muscular process.

evidence.quote: The apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage, the concave base with the cricoid lamina
Triangular pyramids about 15 mm high
The anterior angle of the base is extended by the vocal process

concepts.name: Corniculate cartilage
concepts.definition: A small paired accessory cartilage of the larynx that rests on the apex of the arytenoid cartilage.

evidence.quote: Corniculate: on the apices of the arytenoids
Paired cartilages: are small and comprise: (a) Arytenoid (b) Corniculate (c) Cuneiform

concepts.name: Cuneiform cartilage
concepts.definition: A small paired accessory cartilage of the larynx that lies in the aryepiglottic fold.

evidence.quote: Cuneiform: in the aryepiglottic fold

concepts.name: Vocal process
concepts.definition: The extension of the anterior angle of the base of the arytenoid cartilage, which gives insertion to the vocal ligament.

evidence.quote: The anterior angle of the base extends as the vocal process (insertion of the vocal ligament)
The vocal process gives insertion to the : • Vocal ligament

concepts.name: Muscular process
concepts.definition: The process on the lateral angle of the base of the arytenoid cartilage, on which the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles insert.

evidence.quote: the lateral angle bears the muscular process (insertion of the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles)
The lateral angle presents the muscular process

concepts.name: Cricoarytenoid joint
concepts.definition: The functionally most important joint of the larynx: an elliptical synovial articulation uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina. Its rotatory movement abducts or adducts the vocal cords and its gliding movement closes or opens the posterior part of the glottis.

evidence.quote: An elliptical synovial articulation reinforced by the posterior cricoarytenoid ligament, uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina
Cricoarytenoid joint: rotation abducts and adducts; gliding opens and closes the posterior glottis.
Rotatory movement, in which arytenoid cartilage moves around a vertical axis, thus abducting or adducting the vocal cords

concepts.name: Cricothyroid joint
concepts.definition: A flat synovial joint, reinforced by ligaments, between the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid. Tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis at this joint tenses the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: A flat synovial joint reinforced by ligaments, joining the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid
Cricothyroid joint: tilting tenses the vocal cords.
tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis inducing a tension of the vocal cords

concepts.name: Thyrohyoid membrane
concepts.definition: An extrinsic membrane of the larynx running from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone, with a medial and two lateral thickenings. It is pierced by the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve together with the superior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Thyrohyoid membrane: from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone
The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve pierces it with the superior laryngeal artery

concepts.name: Thyroepiglottic ligament
concepts.definition: An extrinsic ligament of the larynx that attaches the lower narrow end of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle.

evidence.quote: Thyroepiglottic ligament: attaches the lower narrow end of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle
inferior inserts into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage through the thyroepiglottic ligament

concepts.name: Hyoepiglottic ligament
concepts.definition: An extrinsic ligament of the larynx connecting the posterior aspect of the hyoid with the anterior surface of the upper end of the epiglottis.

evidence.quote: Hyoepiglottic ligament: connects the posterior aspect of the hyoid with the anterior surface of the upper end of the epiglottis

concepts.name: Cricotracheal ligament
concepts.definition: An extrinsic ligament of the larynx running between the lower edge of the cricoid and the upper edge of the first tracheal ring.

evidence.quote: Cricotracheal ligament: between the lower edge of the cricoid and the upper edge of the first tracheal ring

concepts.name: Cricothyroid ligament
concepts.definition: A ligament between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages. Stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process it forms the vocal ligament; its median part lies just under the skin between the thyroid cartilage above and the cricoid below, and it bounds the infraglottic cavity.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
The median cricothyroid ligament sits just under the skin between two easily felt landmarks, the thyroid cartilage above and the cricoid below
The median cricothyroid ligament, between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages

concepts.name: Vocal ligament
concepts.definition: An intrinsic ligament of the larynx formed by the cricothyroid ligament stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process of the arytenoid. Together with muscle it makes up the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
made of vocal ligament and muscle

concepts.name: Vestibular ligament
concepts.definition: An intrinsic ligament of the larynx, tense between the thyroid angle and the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid.

evidence.quote: The vestibular ligament is tense between the thyroid angle and the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid

concepts.name: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle
concepts.definition: A muscle of the larynx itself, classed by action as a tensor of the vocal cord, the dilator of the glottis or a constrictor of the glottis. All are paired except the transverse arytenoid, and all are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve except the cricothyroid.

evidence.quote: All the intrinsic muscles are paired except the transverse arytenoid (interarytenoid), which is unpaired
Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid

concepts.name: Cricothyroid muscle
concepts.definition: A paired intrinsic muscle of the larynx, the only one lying on the outer aspect of the larynx and the only one supplied by the external laryngeal nerve. It elevates the cricoid arch and lowers the thyroid cartilage, tensing the vocal cord, and is important for the tone and pitch of the voice.

evidence.quote: Vocal cord tensors: cricothyroid (paired). Action: elevation of the cricoid arch and lowering of the thyroid cartilage, tensing the vocal cord.
Cricothyroid is the only muscle on the outer aspect and the only one on the external laryngeal nerve.
Hence it is also known as the tuning fork of larynx

concepts.name: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: The intrinsic muscle that is the only dilator of the glottis and the only abductor of the vocal cords, inserting on the muscular process of the arytenoid. It is called the safety muscle of the larynx: if it is paralysed the adductors take the upper hand and the person might die from lack of air.

evidence.quote: Posterior cricoarytenoids are the only abductors: the safety muscles of the larynx.
Dilator of the glottis: the posterior cricoarytenoid, the only one.
If posterior cricoarytenoids are paralyzed, the adductor ‘muscles (of vocal cords) take the upper hand and the person might die due to lack of air

concepts.name: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: An intrinsic muscle of the larynx, one of the constrictors of the glottis, that adducts the vocal cords and inserts on the muscular process of the arytenoid.

evidence.quote: Adduct the vocal cords | Lateral cricoarytenoids, transverse arytenoid
Lateral cricoarytenoids: adduct the vocal cords.

concepts.name: Transverse arytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: The only unpaired intrinsic muscle of the larynx, also called the interarytenoid. It inserts on the posterior side of the arytenoid cartilage and adducts the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Transverse arytenoid is the only unpaired intrinsic muscle.
the posterior side takes the transverse arytenoid muscle
Transverse arytenoid: adduct the vocal cords.

concepts.name: Thyroarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: An intrinsic muscle of the larynx listed among the constrictors of the glottis, with a superior part running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the lower third of the arytenoid and an inferior part, the vocal muscle. It relaxes the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Relax the vocal cords | Thyroarytenoid
superior thyroarytenoid (from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the lower third of the arytenoid)
Thyroarytenoid: relaxes the vocal cords

concepts.name: Vocalis muscle
concepts.definition: The inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle, running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid. It tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle (from the reentrant angle to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid), which tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the cord
Tense the vocal cords | Cricothyroid, vocalis

concepts.name: Extrinsic laryngeal muscle
concepts.definition: A muscle that ensures laryngeal mobility, especially during swallowing. The elevators are the thyrohyoid, mylohyoid and digastric; the depressors are the sternothyroid, sternohyoid and omohyoid.

evidence.quote: Extrinsic muscles ensure laryngeal mobility, especially during swallowing. Elevators: thyrohyoid, mylohyoid, digastric. Depressors: sternothyroid, sternohyoid, omohyoid.
Extrinsic muscles: ensure laryngeal mobility especially during swallowing

concepts.name: Vocal fold
concepts.definition: One of two pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle. The vocal cords are covered by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium and have no lymphatics.

evidence.quote: Two pearly white vocal cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle
Vocal cords have stratified squamous epithelium and no lymphatics.
Vocal cords: 2 pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid cartilage in back

concepts.name: Vestibular fold
concepts.definition: The false vocal cord or ventricular band. The vestibule lies above the vestibular folds and the laryngeal ventricle lies between them and the vocal folds.

evidence.quote: between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below
vestibule above the vestibular folds, ventricle between them and the vocal folds

concepts.name: Glottis
concepts.definition: The compartment of the larynx delimited by the two vocal cords, triangular in shape and narrower than the vestibular cleft. It is the narrowest part in adults and a narrow zone in children, where obstructive oedema causes respiratory distress very rapidly.

evidence.quote: The glottis is triangular and narrower than the vestibular cleft
The glottis is the narrowest part in adults.
Glottis: delimited by the 2 vocal cords, it is triangular in shape.

concepts.name: Rima glottidis
concepts.definition: The opening between the vocal cords, through which air passes when the cords are abducted.

evidence.quote: abduct the vocal cords, letting air through the rima glottidis
The gap between the vocal cords

concepts.name: Laryngeal vestibule
concepts.definition: A pyramidal space of the supraglottic compartment extending from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands, that is, the space above the vestibular folds.

evidence.quote: Vestibule: a pyramidal space from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands
Spaces: vestibule above the vestibular folds
Vestibule of larynx — space above

concepts.name: Laryngeal ventricle
concepts.definition: The cavity between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below.

evidence.quote: Laryngeal or Morgagni ventricle: between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below
ventricle between them and the vocal folds

concepts.name: Infraglottic cavity
concepts.definition: The cavity of the larynx below the vocal cords, surrounded by the cricoid and the cricothyroid ligament.

evidence.quote: The cavity below the vocal cords, surrounded by the cricoid and the cricothyroid ligament
Infraglottic cavity — space inferior to vocal folds

concepts.name: Supraglottis
concepts.definition: The compartment of the larynx above the glottis, comprising the vestibule, the laryngeal ventricle and the interarytenoid region. It is very rich in lymphatics.

evidence.quote: Supraglottic | Vestibule: a pyramidal space from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands
Very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent at the vocal cords

concepts.name: Anterior commissure
concepts.definition: The point where the two vocal cords unite anteriorly, attached directly to the thyroid cartilage and containing vessels and lymphatics.

evidence.quote: Anteriorly they unite at the anterior commissure, attached directly to the thyroid cartilage and containing vessels and lymphatics
unite to form the Anterior Commissure, directly attached to the thyroid cartilage containing vessels and lymphatics

concepts.name: Aryepiglottic fold
concepts.definition: A fold of mucosa going from the epiglottis to the arytenoid cartilage; it contains the cuneiform cartilage.

evidence.quote: Aryepiglottic fold — folds of mucosa going from epiglottis to arytenoid cartilage
Cuneiform: in the aryepiglottic fold

concepts.name: Laryngeal mucosa
concepts.definition: The thin, smooth, pale pink lining of the larynx, continuous above with the pharyngeal mucosa and below with the tracheal mucosa. Its epithelium is respiratory type throughout, except at the vocal cords and the upper half of the epiglottis, which are non-keratinized stratified squamous.

evidence.quote: The epithelium is respiratory type (cylindric stratified) throughout, except at the vocal cords and the upper half of the epiglottis, which are non-keratinized stratified squamous
Epithelium is respiratory except at the vocal cords and upper half of the epiglottis: stratified squamous.
Non-keratinized stratified squamous type at the vocal cords and the upper ½ of the epiglottis

concepts.name: Superior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the superior thyroid artery that supplies the supraglottic part of the larynx and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery. It enters the larynx through the thyrohyoid membrane with the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery. Supplies the supraglottic part and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery
Superior Laryngeal Artery (SLA): branch of the Superior Thyroid Artery, it vascularizes the supraglottic part

concepts.name: Anteroinferior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the superior thyroid artery that supplies the anterior part of the infraglottic stage of the larynx.

evidence.quote: Anteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery. Supplies the anterior part of the infraglottic stage
Anteroinferior Laryngeal Artery (ALAI): branch of the Superior Thyroid Artery, it vascularizes the anterior part of the infraglottic stage

concepts.name: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the inferior thyroid artery that supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa and anastomoses with the superior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the inferior thyroid artery. Supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa
Posteroinferior Laryngeal Artery (ALPI): branch of the Inferior Thyroid Artery. It vascularizes the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa

concepts.name: Superior thyroid artery
concepts.definition: The artery that gives off the superior laryngeal artery and the anteroinferior laryngeal artery to the larynx.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery
Anteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery

concepts.name: Inferior thyroid artery
concepts.definition: The artery that gives off the posteroinferior laryngeal artery to the larynx.

evidence.quote: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the inferior thyroid artery

concepts.name: Laryngeal vein
concepts.definition: A vein of the larynx, satellite to the arteries. The superior and inferior laryngeal veins drain to the superior thyroid vein, then the thyro-linguo-facial trunk, then the internal jugular vein; the posterior laryngeal vein drains to the inferior thyroid vein, then the subclavian vein.

evidence.quote: Superior and inferior laryngeal veins to the superior thyroid vein, then the thyro-linguo-facial trunk, then the internal jugular vein
Posterior laryngeal vein to the inferior thyroid vein, then the subclavian vein

concepts.name: Lymphatic drainage of the larynx
concepts.definition: The lymphatics of the larynx are very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone and absent at the vocal cords. The supraglottic region drains to the internal jugular chain; the infraglottic region drains to pretracheal and paratracheal nodes and the internal jugular chain.

evidence.quote: Very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent at the vocal cords
Lymphatics are absent at the vocal cords, rich supraglottically.
Very rich in the supraglottic zones, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent in the vocal cords

concepts.name: Internal jugular lymph node
concepts.definition: A node of the internal jugular chain, which receives the lymph of the supraglottic region of the larynx and, together with pretracheal and paratracheal nodes, that of the infraglottic region.

evidence.quote: Supraglottic: the internal jugular chain. Infraglottic: pretracheal and paratracheal nodes and the internal jugular chain
Supraglottic region → internal jugular chain

concepts.name: Vagus nerve
concepts.definition: The nerve whose branches, the superior laryngeal nerve and the recurrent laryngeal nerve, innervate the larynx.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal nerve | A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory
From the vagus, on the right at the base of the neck and on the left at the thorax

concepts.name: Superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, that descends against the pharyngeal wall and divides behind the greater horn of the hyoid into an internal and an external branch.

evidence.quote: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, descending against the pharyngeal wall and dividing behind the greater horn of the hyoid
It divides behind the greater horn of the hyoid into two branches

concepts.name: Internal laryngeal nerve
aliases: internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. It enters the larynx with the superior laryngeal artery by perforating the thyrohyoid membrane and gives sensory innervation to the supraglottic mucosa, above the vocal folds, plus autonomic fibres.

evidence.quote: Enters the larynx with the superior laryngeal artery by perforating the thyrohyoid membrane. Sensory innervation of the supraglottic mucosa, plus autonomic fibres
Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve: sensation above the cords, piercing the thyrohyoid membrane.
Pierces thyrohyoid membrane + Sensory from mucosa above vocal folds

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve
aliases: external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. It innervates the cricothyroid muscle and perforates the cricothyroid membrane; the lecture also gives it sensory innervation of the subglottic stage.

evidence.quote: External branch | Innervates the cricothyroid muscle and perforates the cricothyroid membrane; sensory innervation of the subglottic stage
External branch - innervates cricothyroid m

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: A branch of the vagus arising on the right at the base of the neck and on the left in the thorax. It is motor to all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid and sensory below the vocal folds. The left nerve loops under the aortic arch and the right under the subclavian artery.

evidence.quote: Motor to all the intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid; sensory below the vocal folds through an ascending branch anastomosing with the superior laryngeal nerve
Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid, and sensation below the cords.
The left recurrent nerve loops under the aortic arch (long course → more often damaged by chest disease); the right loops under the subclavian artery.

concepts.name: Phonation
concepts.definition: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy. The sound produced is then modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants.

evidence.quote: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy
The phonation (speech) is produced by the vibrations of the vocal cords

concepts.name: Acoustic parameters of the voice
concepts.definition: The three parameters that characterise the voice: frequency, in Hertz, depending on the vibration speed of the vocal folds; intensity, in dB, depending on the force of pulmonary expiration (subglottic pressure); and pitch, depending on the accommodation of the vocal folds but especially on the shape of the supralaryngeal cavities.

evidence.quote: The voice is characterised by three acoustic parameters: frequency, in Hertz, depending on the vibration speed of the vocal folds
Voice parameters: frequency (Hz), intensity (dB), pitch.
The voice is characterized by 3 acoustic parameters

concepts.name: Vibratory cycle of the vocal folds
concepts.definition: The three-step cycle of phonation: the folds close as the arytenoids come together (phonatory position); they open when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, letting a puff of air pass at high speed as an acoustic impulse; then the folds close again.

evidence.quote: Putting into phonatory position: the folds close as the arytenoids come together
when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, a puff of air passes at high speed, an acoustic impulse

concepts.name: Supralaryngeal cavity
concepts.definition: An air cavity above the larynx, notably the pharynx and the oral cavity, that modifies and filters the laryngeal sound by resonance, enriching some frequencies and suppressing others, and takes part in articulation.

evidence.quote: The sound produced is immediately modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants: the bucco-pharyngeal resonators
Filter role: resonance and enrichment of certain frequencies or suppression of others, with two areas of particular enhancement, the pharynx and the oral cavity

concepts.name: Vocal fold abduction
concepts.definition: The movement that opens the vocal cords and lets air through the rima glottidis. It is produced only by the posterior cricoarytenoids: the muscular processes of both arytenoids rotate medially and the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening.

evidence.quote: When they contract, the muscular processes of both arytenoids rotate medially and the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening
Abduct the vocal cords | Posterior cricoarytenoids

concepts.name: Vocal fold adduction
concepts.definition: The movement that brings the vocal cords together, produced by the lateral cricoarytenoids and the transverse arytenoid. The cords are kept adducted for phonation.

evidence.quote: Adduct the vocal cords | Lateral cricoarytenoids, transverse arytenoid
The vocal cords are kept adducted

concepts.name: Vocal fold tension
concepts.definition: The tensing or relaxing of the vocal cords. The cricothyroid and vocalis tense them, as does tilting of the cricoid at the cricothyroid joint; the thyroarytenoid relaxes them.

evidence.quote: Tense: cricothyroid and vocalis. Relax: thyroarytenoid.
Tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis (arch up, lamina down) tenses the vocal cords

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve, often accidental during partial thyroidectomy. Unilaterally, the cord on the affected side lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates; bilaterally, both cords lie paramedian with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, often damaged accidentally during partial thyroidectomy: unilaterally, the cord lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates
bilaterally, both cords lie paramedian with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing
Unilateral recurrent laryngeal palsy (thyroidectomy, left-sided aortic or lung lesions): hoarse voice, cord paramedian. Bilateral: stridor, airway emergency.

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Damage to the external laryngeal nerve, causing weakness of phonation from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid: a weak, monotone voice that cannot reach high notes, especially noticeable in singers.

evidence.quote: External laryngeal nerve: weakness of phonation from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid
External laryngeal injury (superior thyroid artery ligation): weak, monotone voice, can't reach high notes.

concepts.name: Cadaveric position of the vocal cords
concepts.definition: The position in which the vocal cords are further abducted and fixed because all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed, seen when both the recurrent and the external laryngeal nerves are damaged on both sides.

evidence.quote: all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed and the cords are further abducted and fixed: the cadaveric position
Bilateral with external nerve: cadaveric position.
This is known as the cadaveric postion of vocal cords or rma

concepts.name: Paramedian position of the vocal cord
concepts.definition: A position of the vocal cord between abduction and adduction, in which the cord of the affected side lies and does not vibrate after damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

evidence.quote: Unilateral recurrent nerve palsy: paramedian cord.
lies in paramedian position (between ‘abduction and adduction) and does not vibrate
the cord on the affected side lies in the paramedian position, between abduction and adduction, and does not vibrate

concepts.name: Vocal nodule
concepts.definition: An inflammatory nodule that develops in people who overuse the voice at the junction of the anterior one third and posterior two thirds of the vocal cords, the area of maximum contact during vibration. The nodules are bilateral and symmetrical, pin head to split pea in size, soft, reddish and oedematous early and later greyish or whitish.

evidence.quote: The area of maximum contact during vibration is at the junction of the anterior one third and posterior two thirds of the cords
Vocal nodules form at the junction of the anterior third and posterior two thirds of the cords.
the inflammatory nodules develop at these sites called vocal nodules

concepts.name: Laryngeal obstruction
concepts.definition: Obstruction of the larynx by a foreign body. The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body normally causes immediate explosive coughing; if that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows.

evidence.quote: The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body causes immediate explosive coughing. If that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows.

concepts.name: Heimlich manoeuvre
concepts.definition: A manoeuvre to relieve choking: standing behind the victim with the arms passed under theirs and the hands in front of the epigastrium, one as a fist and the other over it, three or four abdominal thrusts are given upwards and backwards, squeezing the residual air up to dislodge the foreign body.

evidence.quote: give three or four abdominal thrusts directed upwards and backwards, squeezing the residual air up to dislodge the foreign body
a foreign body may enter and cause choking. The Heimlich manoeuvre relieves it

concepts.name: Thyroidectomy
concepts.definition: An operation, named in the lecture as partial thyroidectomy, during which the recurrent laryngeal nerve is often damaged accidentally.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, often damaged accidentally during partial thyroidectomy

concepts.name: Cricothyroidotomy
concepts.definition: An emergency airway made through the cricothyroid membrane, between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages, a superficial and relatively avascular spot.

evidence.quote: Emergency airway: cricothyroidotomy goes through the cricothyroid membrane (between thyroid and cricoid), a superficial, relatively avascular spot.

concepts.name: Hyoid bone
concepts.definition: The U-shaped bone above the larynx, to whose lower edge the thyrohyoid membrane attaches. It is closely associated with the larynx but is usually considered a separate structure.

evidence.quote: Above: the hyoid bone and base of the tongue
Hyoid bone: the U-shaped bone above the larynx.

Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid, and sensation below the cords.

notes: Slides 37 and 64 are scanned textbook pages with heavy OCR errors and missing words; slide 53 is only figure labels. Quotes from them are copied as they appear, errors included.

The packet uses 'vocal cord' and 'vocal fold', 'vestibular fold', 'ventricular band' and 'false vocal cord', and 'cricothyroid ligament' and 'cricothyroid membrane' interchangeably; each group is treated as one concept with the other terms as aliases.
'Lymphatic drainage of the larynx' is classed as a process for want of a better kind; it describes the distribution and destination of the laryngeal lymphatics.

In q:ciq1vx the note on distractor A ('Both cords become fixed in abduction — That is bilateral palsy') does not say whether it means bilateral recurrent palsy alone, for which the text gives the paramedian position, or combined recurrent and external nerve damage; not listed as a conflict.
The text says lymphatics are absent at the vocal cords but also that the anterior commissure, where the cords unite, contains vessels and lymphatics; reported here rather than as a conflict.

Several figure questions and cards (hyoid bone, trachea, laryngeal prominence) are supported mainly by the question or card text itself, since the lecture sections mention these structures only in passing.
